description: Vote load test: 750 synthetic pools voting from 10 leiosred block producers (76 BLS keys each). Compares vote volume, certification health and network egress against a baseline window one $baseline earlier. The three leios[1-3]-bp hosts keep a single real key and act as the untouched control.

panels.description: Each leiosred block producer carries 76 BLS keys; the three leios[1-3]-bp hosts carry one and are the control. Votes only exist while there are transactions to endorse, so the signal tracks the tx-generator duty cycle.
panels.title: Votes cast per minute, by host — 10 leiosred loaders vs 3 control BPs

panels.description: The same data collapsed to two series. The control line staying flat through the step is what proves the extra volume is the synthetic keys and not a network-wide change.
panels.title: Load vs control

panels.description: Every host in the environment, including relays, dbsync, faucet, metsuke and centrifuge. These hosts cast nothing — a step here means the synthetic votes reached the whole network, and tightly bunched lines mean diffusion is even.
panels.title: Votes acquired per second — all 26 hosts (diffusion reach)

panels.description: Vote rate over the last $window divided by the same length of time one $baseline earlier.
panels.title: Vote multiplier vs baseline

panels.description: Distinct voterId label values currently reporting. 15 at rest, 765 with the synthetic keys loaded. This is also the added Mimir series cost — voterId is promoted on votes_cast_total and voted_weight_total.
panels.title: Voting identities (series cost)

panels.description: Votes the node scheduled but declined to cast. A climb here under load means the voting path is shedding work.
panels.title: Votes declined / s (fleet)
Certification — expected to be unchanged (synthetic seats carry zero weight)

panels.description: Live view of distance to quorum. NOT a valid before/after comparator under heavy vote load: the tally histogram records one sample per vote arrival, so 15x the votes means 15x denser sampling of the accumulation curve and the mean falls mechanically. Measured 158k tally updates/h unloaded against 2.7M/h loaded. Use certified-per-forged EB for certification health instead.
panels.title: Vote tally vs quorum threshold

panels.description: Certified and forged endorser blocks seen by one block producer. Selects on the indexed kind label; that stream holds one copy per event, so no halving is applied.
panels.title: Endorser blocks certified and forged (leios1-bp-a-1)

panels.description: Absolute transmit rate per relay, loopback excluded. These are the highest-degree hosts in the environment at roughly 90-145 duplex connections each.
panels.title: Relay egress, per host

panels.description: Absolute transmit rate per block producer. The three leios[1-3]-bp control hosts sit near 70-90 KB/s throughout; the leiosred loaders are the ones casting 76x the votes.
panels.title: Block producer egress, per host

panels.description: Aggregate egress by role. Votes are small; if they cost meaningful bandwidth it shows up here first.
panels.title: Fleet egress by role (stacked)

panels.description: Relay receive rate. Under the vote load this is the side that actually moved — relays ingest every synthetic vote, where egress is dominated by block and header serving.
panels.title: Relay ingress, per host
Peak egress — this window vs one $baseline earlier

panels.description: Peak and mean egress per host. Peaks use irate() on the raw counter, which at this cluster's 60-second scrape yields a true 1-minute rate — roughly 1.5x higher than the rate5m recording rules, and still only 10-18% of the real 1-second peak. For burst questions use each host's local netdata (localhost:19999, 1s resolution, ~96h retention), not this panel. Means are exact at any window length. Connection counts are shown because relay egress tracks peer degree far more strongly than vote volume: a large ratio next to a large connection swing is topology churn, not vote cost.
panels.title: Peak (1-minute) and mean egress per host, before vs after

panels.description: Node process CPU. This moves more than bandwidth does under vote load — verification, not transmission, is the binding cost.
panels.title: Relay node CPU (cores)

panels.description: Mux errors on relays, split by peer. The loopback series is the node's own per-minute cli ping and should stay flat; a rising remote series is genuine connection churn against external peers. Selects on the indexed kind label rather than a line filter over the full cardano-node stream, which is ~11.7M lines/hour across these 9 relays. The indexed stream holds one copy per event, so no halving is applied here.
panels.title: Relay mux errors — remote vs loopback

list.name: window
list.label: Comparison window
list.description: Length of the before and after windows used by the stat and table panels.

list.name: baseline
list.label: Baseline offset
list.description: How far back the comparison window sits. The transaction generator runs a one-hour on/off duty cycle and votes only exist while it is on, so this must be an even number of hours to compare like with like.
